coverage_statement: Targeted evidence map, not exhaustive systematic review; 40 records include reviews and methods, not 40 independent yield experiments.

studies.title: The value of bees to the coffee harvest
studies.source_locator: Indexed article sections: methods/results/discussion; supplements not fully extracted
studies.reported_design: Panama; 50 two-year-old arabica plants; open and fine-mesh-bagged control branches.
studies.reported_results: Open branches produced 49% more ripe berries per flower and mean berries were 7% heavier.
studies.reported_analysis: Paired t-test reported for berry abundance.
studies.project_interpretation: Use matched branch cohorts and mature harvest outcomes; this does not isolate our stingless colony.

studies.title: Bee pollination and fruit set of Coffea arabica and C. canephora (Rubiaceae)
studies.source_locator: Indexed article sections: methods/results/discussion; supplements not fully extracted
studies.reported_design: 24 Indonesian agroforestry fields; insect/wind/self and hand-cross comparisons across both crop species.
studies.reported_results: Canephora fruit set: open 78.1%, hand cross 83.8%, wind plus self 62.3%; open and hand cross were not significantly different.
studies.project_interpretation: Store treatment mechanism and species; 78.1 minus 62.3 is 15.8 percentage points, not 15.8% relative gain.

studies.title: Fruit set of highland coffee increases with the diversity of pollinating bees
studies.source_locator: Abstract
studies.reported_design: 24 Indonesian arabica agroforestry systems plus single-visit experiments.
studies.reported_results: Fruit set ranged roughly 60–90% across a bee-richness gradient of 3–20 species; some rare solitary visitors outperformed abundant social species per visit.
studies.project_interpretation: Do not replace functional performance with total bee counts; landscape richness relationships are not randomized richness treatments.

studies.title: Pollination of Coffea canephora in relation to local and regional agroforestry management
studies.source_locator: Abstract
studies.reported_design: 15 Sulawesi agroforestry systems; bee surveys, bagged/open treatments and pollination efficiency of 15 bee species.
studies.reported_results: Open fruit set increased with bee diversity/abundance; solitary assemblages provided higher per-visit fruit set than social assemblages.
studies.project_interpretation: Record habitat, visitor identity and visitation effort; check overlap with other Klein datasets before synthesis.

studies.title: Economic value of tropical forest to coffee production
studies.source_locator: Abstract
studies.reported_design: Costa Rica; pollination experiments along replicated forest-distance gradients.
studies.reported_results: Estimated forest-linked yield benefit 20% within about 1 km; peaberry frequency reduced 27%; historical valuation about USD60,000/year for one farm.
studies.project_interpretation: Retain distance, seed form and valuation assumptions; these historical dollar estimates are not our projected revenue.

studies.title: Pollinator diversity increases fruit production in Mexican coffee plantations: The importance of rustic management systems
studies.source_locator: Abstract
studies.reported_design: Central Veracruz management gradient; observational and experimental measurements of diversity and production.
studies.reported_results: Lower-impact systems had greater visitor richness/diversity and higher fruit production; positive diversity-production associations were reported.
studies.project_interpretation: Management and landscape covariates need separate fields; do not assume their observational association identifies one causal mechanism.

studies.title: Status of pollinators and their efficiency in coffee fruit set in a fragmented landscape mosaic in South India
studies.source_locator: Indexed article sections: methods/results/discussion; supplements not fully extracted
studies.reported_design: Kodagu robusta; self, no-pollination, wind, open and hand-cross treatments; visitor observations.
studies.reported_results: Final fruit set: cross 44%, open 33%, wind 22.1%; five-week initial set was unreliable for final set.
studies.project_interpretation: Keep initial and final outcomes separate and include positive hand-cross comparisons when measuring deficits.

studies.title: Interactive effects among ecosystem services and management practices on crop production: Pollination in coffee agroforestry systems
studies.source_locator: Indexed article sections: methods/results/discussion; supplements not fully extracted
studies.reported_design: Indian coffee systems; bee abundance, irrigation-induced flowering, shade, lime and environmental variables considered together.
studies.reported_results: Bee abundance benefited production after accounting for management; irrigation and liming effects could exceed shade-cover effects.
studies.project_interpretation: Log irrigation and flowering synchrony; cameras at a busy flowering patch cannot alone identify a hive effect.

studies.title: Complementary ecosystem services provided by pest predators and pollinators increase quantity and quality of coffee yields
studies.source_locator: Indexed article sections: methods/results/discussion; supplements not fully extracted
studies.reported_design: 180 coffee bushes, Kilimanjaro land-use gradient; vertebrate × pollinator exclusions. Gauze apertures 0.39 × 0.77 mm; strings kept fabric away from flowers.
studies.reported_results: Pollinators did not significantly change fruit set but increased fruit weight 7.4%; vertebrate exclusion reduced set about 9%.
studies.reported_analysis: Binomial responses for set/retention; mixed-effects analyses with hierarchical units.
studies.project_interpretation: Measure mass as well as set; a published coffee mesh cannot be transferred to cacao midges without qualification.

studies.title: Landscape structure influences bee community and coffee pollination at different spatial scales
studies.source_locator: Indexed article sections: methods/results/discussion; supplements not fully extracted
studies.reported_design: Brazil; nine landscapes, 15 arabica shrubs each, floral exclusions and visitor surveys; 300 m, 1 km and 2 km landscape scales.
studies.reported_results: Authors reported 28% greater fruit set with bees; community relationships differed by spatial scale.
studies.project_interpretation: Store buffer radius with every landscape metric; do not average scales or interpret this reported percentage as percentage points.

studies.title: Performance, Effectiveness, and Efficiency of Honeybees as Pollinators of Coffea arabica (Gentianales, Rubiaceae)
studies.source_locator: Abstract
studies.reported_design: Bahia; open, wind, hand cross and single-visit bee treatments; pollen deposition, pollen tubes and fruit formation.
studies.reported_results: Single visits transferred pollen; deposition quantity did not differ among treatments, while hand cross and single visits showed greater fertilization measures.
studies.project_interpretation: A counted pollen grain and a fertilizing pollen tube are different endpoints; optional microscopy requires a separate sampling cohort.

studies.title: Interacting pest control and pollination services in coffee systems
studies.source_locator: Indexed article sections: methods/results/discussion; supplements not fully extracted
studies.reported_design: 30 Costa Rican farms; eight plants/farm; bird exclusion using 20 mm mesh and bee exclusion using 1 mm nylon branch bags installed before bloom and removed after.
studies.reported_results: Joint bird/bee exclusion reduced estimated yield 24.7%; positive interactions affected set, mass and uniformity.
studies.reported_analysis: Models tested bird × bee treatments and fruit condition/time; hierarchical design.
studies.project_interpretation: Support nested factorial designs and interaction terms; this is a combined-services result, not a bee-only yield estimate.

studies.title: Bee pollination affects coffee quality, yield, and trade-offs within them
studies.source_locator: Abstract
studies.reported_design: 30 plants in Tarrazú, Costa Rica; bee exclusions, harvest measurements and certified cuppers; online 2024, journal volume 2025.
studies.reported_results: Authors reported fruit set +9%, aroma +2%, berry mass −7%, with body/balance trade-offs.
studies.project_interpretation: Archive processing and blind cupping batches; improved set does not imply every quality attribute improves.

studies.title: Managed Africanized honey bees and native stingless bees increase Arabica coffee yields in southeastern Brazil
studies.source_locator: Abstract
studies.reported_design: Managed Apis and Scaptotrigona introduced in 23 coffee fields; nearby versus more distant comparisons.
studies.reported_results: Yield per bush increased 16% near colonies; stingless-bee effects had higher variability with low replication.
studies.project_interpretation: Useful colony-addition precedent; identify spillover and background colony confounding. Check dataset overlap with C15.

studies.title: Stingless bees in coffee: yield gains and assessing neonicotinoid impact
studies.source_locator: Indexed article sections: methods/results/discussion; supplements not fully extracted
studies.reported_design: Brazil; Scaptotrigona depilis, conventional/organic farms; near <50 m versus 200–300 m; 360 harvested branches across six yield-study farms.
studies.reported_results: Near-colony branches yielded 67% more; measured colony endpoints did not show significant adverse effects under the studied exposure.
studies.project_interpretation: Do not infer universal pesticide safety or guaranteed gains; distinguish branch outcomes from C14 bush outcomes. Published January 6, 2026 despite the 2025 DOI suffix.

studies.title: Nocturnal insect communities altered by land-use change contribute little to coffee pollination in the Western Ghats, India
studies.source_locator: Abstract
studies.reported_design: Robusta; day/night floral access and community sampling with light screens in agroforest/secondary forest; volume 2026, online 2025.
studies.reported_results: Diurnal contribution dominated; nocturnal effect absent in agroforest, with some evidence in secondary forest.
studies.project_interpretation: Treat lighting/traps as sampling interventions; quantify local diel activity before deciding to omit nights.

studies.title: Energy costs of flowering, fruiting, and cherelle wilt in cacao
studies.source_locator: Abstract
studies.reported_design: Fourteen-year-old trees: hand pollination, natural pollination and fruit removal; 1983–1986 tracking of flowers, cherelles, pods and biochemical composition.
studies.reported_results: Hand pollination produced more cherelles but not significantly more mature fruits because wilting increased.
studies.project_interpretation: A required counterexample to early-set yield claims; maintain competing fruit-loss outcomes.

studies.title: Effect of pollination intensity on fruit and seed set in cacao (Theobroma cacao L.)
studies.source_locator: Abstract
studies.reported_design: Ivory Coast, clone UPA409; deposited pollen related to pod survival and seeds; styles counted after cutting 24 hours post-pollination.
studies.reported_results: Dose-response and saturation in fruit/seed outcomes; published thresholds were specific to the tested material.
studies.project_interpretation: Do not encode a universal minimum pollen count; destructive style sampling needs a validated crop/genotype procedure.

studies.title: Experimental evidence for stronger cacao yield limitation by pollination than by plant resources
studies.source_locator: Indexed article sections: methods/results/discussion; supplements not fully extracted
studies.reported_design: Sulawesi; 10/40/70/100% hand pollination of accessible flowers up to 2 m, crossed with resource treatments in two experiments.
studies.reported_results: Yield rose nonlinearly to about twice current levels; largest change was 10→40%; tested resource effects were nonsignificant.
studies.project_interpretation: Accessible-flower denominator matters; twice baseline is +100%, not +200%, and is not a universal optimum.

studies.title: Increased pollinator habitat enhances cacao fruit set and predator conservation
studies.source_locator: Abstract
studies.reported_design: Cacao husk additions crossed with pollen supplementation; pollination and predator responses measured.
studies.reported_results: Husks increased fruits per tree; supplementation/habitat treatments improved final yield, while spider/skink densities also increased.
studies.project_interpretation: Habitat manipulation is a distinct treatment; source/disease status, substrate mass and maintenance must be logged. Online 2016, issue 2017.

studies.title: Supplemental and synchronized pollination may increase yield in cacao
studies.source_locator: Abstract
studies.reported_design: Three high-yielding clones; donor genotype, pollination intensity and synchrony manipulated.
studies.reported_results: Supplementation improved yield; donor and cherelle age mattered; pollination intensity did not significantly change harvested yield.
studies.project_interpretation: Track donor-recipient pair, cohort ages and intensity independently; increasing labor does not guarantee increased harvest.

studies.title: Hand pollination, not pesticides or fertilizers, increases cocoa yields and farmer income
studies.source_locator: Indexed article sections: methods/results/discussion; supplements not fully extracted
studies.reported_design: Sulawesi; partial trial used 128 trees, accessible flowers over 60 days; pollination compared with agrochemical inputs, plus full-pollination trial.
studies.reported_results: Reported yield increases 51% for 13% partial pollination and 161% for full pollination; study-specific net-income increase about 69%.
studies.project_interpretation: Record labor/opportunity costs and intervention coverage. These are separate treatment comparisons, not one universal response curve.

studies.title: Impact of insecticide and pollinator-enhancing substrate applications on cocoa (Theobroma cacao) cherelle and pod production in Côte d’Ivoire
studies.source_locator: Indexed article sections: methods/results/discussion; supplements not fully extracted
studies.reported_design: Three farms; banana pseudostems with/without insecticide and distance comparisons; 25-week observation period.
studies.reported_results: Some treatments increased cherelles, but accumulated mature pod numbers did not significantly increase.
studies.project_interpretation: Do not convert substrate-related early set into yield or recommend insecticide from this result.

studies.title: Cacao flower visitation: Low pollen deposition, low fruit set and dominance of herbivores
studies.source_locator: Indexed article sections: methods/results/discussion; supplements not fully extracted
studies.reported_design: Peruvian cacao; sticky-glue flower visitor sampling, pollen assessment and separate hand-pollination comparison.
studies.reported_results: Natural set 39/1952 (~2%); hand pollination 70/968 (~7%), assessed as healthy cherelles six days later; visitor composition differed regionally.
studies.project_interpretation: Trap counts, video visits and six-day set are distinct measures; do not use sticky-treated flowers as undisturbed yield cohorts.

studies.title: Quantifying services and disservices provided by insects and vertebrates in cacao agroforestry landscapes
studies.source_locator: Indexed article sections: methods/results/discussion; supplements not fully extracted
studies.reported_design: Northwestern Peru, 12 agroforests; flying insects, ants, birds and bats excluded in factorial combinations, about one year follow-up.
studies.reported_results: Open set averaged 1.7%, flying-insect exclusion 0.3%; bird/bat access more than doubled yield; fruit predation caused additional losses.
studies.project_interpretation: Maintain separate access factors and loss causes. One exclusion bag is not a taxon-specific experiment unless its permeability is verified.

studies.title: Cross-pollination with native genotypes improves fruit set and yield quality of Peruvian cacao
studies.source_locator: Abstract
studies.reported_design: Self-pollen versus five native donor genotypes; microclimate and seed outcomes considered.
studies.reported_results: Self-pollination success 0.5%; cross-pollination 3–8 times higher; donor identity mattered and supplemented fruits had higher seed weight/premium content.
studies.project_interpretation: Store compatibility and donor identity rather than only hand_pollinated=true; do not interpret 3–8-fold as high absolute success.

studies.title: Global chocolate supply is limited by low pollination and high temperatures
studies.source_locator: Indexed article sections: methods/results/discussion; supplements not fully extracted
studies.reported_design: Hand-pollination experiments in Brazil (10 sites), Ghana (8) and Indonesia (8), with tree/site/climate covariates.
studies.reported_results: Reported hand-pollination yield benefit 20%; temperature and tree/soil-related covariates also explained variation.
studies.project_interpretation: Preserve region and experiment identity; verify overlap with earlier Indonesian experiments before treating effects as independent.

studies.title: Not all flowers' visitors are pollinators: Combining indicators to identify their role in the cocoa pollination service
studies.record_type: controlled trial and video field study
studies.source_locator: Abstract
studies.reported_design: Controlled pollen quantity/quality trial plus transects/video in Ecuador and indicators of visitor contribution.
studies.reported_results: Pollen quantity drove fruit-set/ovule responses; crawling arthropods including ants/aphids were identified as promising contributors in that context.
studies.project_interpretation: Store evidence per claim, region and method; do not collapse this finding and K13 into a universal visitor whitelist.

studies.title: Revisiting cacao pollination: new behavioural and pollen-based evidence for the key role of Ceratopogonidae
studies.source_locator: Indexed article sections: methods/results/discussion; supplements not fully extracted
studies.reported_design: Malaysia/French Guiana; randomized 10-minute sessions, aspirator sampling, microclimate, microscopy and subset barcoding. Pollen checked fresh before ethanol.
studies.reported_results: Forcipomyia were strongest candidates; 43% of Malaysian biting midges carried cacao pollen. Visit-specific fertilization was not directly measured.
studies.reported_analysis: Chi-square behavioural comparisons; Welch temperature and rank-based humidity comparisons.
studies.project_interpretation: Preserve specimen processing order and distinction between compatible behaviour and demonstrated effectiveness.

studies.title: 3D pollination biology using micro-computed tomography and geometric morphometrics in Theobroma cacao
studies.source_locator: Indexed article sections: methods/results/discussion; supplements not fully extracted
studies.reported_design: Micro-CT of flowers and potential visitors; landmark geometry with 3D Slicer and geomorph; floral entry dimensions compared with insect bodies.
studies.reported_results: Floral access geometry separated potential visitors into differing morphological suitability classes.
studies.reported_analysis: Geometric morphometric analysis; body/floral dimension comparison.
studies.project_interpretation: Microscopy/CT can support hypotheses but is not a visit-to-fruit experiment; outsource specialist imaging instead of buying CT for the pilot.

studies.title: Identifying Cocoa Flower Visitors: A Deep Learning Dataset
studies.source_locator: Abstract
studies.reported_design: Hainan embedded-camera data; 5,792 insect images and 1,082 background images curated from 23 million images; five visitor groups.
studies.reported_results: Best reported tested configuration: YOLOv8 medium, F1 0.71 and mAP50 0.70.
studies.project_interpretation: Use published 2025 version, not 2024 preprint as a second study. Family/group labels and detection metrics are not species accuracy or proof of pollination.

studies.title: Caveats to quantifying ecosystem services: fruit abortion blurs benefits from crop pollination
studies.source_locator: Abstract
studies.reported_design: Coffee in Ecuador, cacao in Indonesia and passion fruit in Brazil; pollination benefits followed toward harvested fruit.
studies.reported_results: Reproductive strategies and environmental stress can obscure initial benefits from enhanced pollination.
studies.project_interpretation: Retain complete cohort fate and final harvest; never value early fruit set as guaranteed saleable yield.

studies.title: The value of biotic pollination and dense forest for fruit set of Arabica coffee: A global assessment
studies.source_locator: Indexed article sections: methods/results/discussion; supplements not fully extracted
studies.reported_design: Eleven case studies/182 samples; open/excluded set and landscape remote sensing.
studies.reported_results: Pooled open set averaged about 65%, excluded about 55%; dense-forest relationships had restricted supporting coverage.
studies.project_interpretation: Retain baseline rates and heterogeneity; do not add this synthesis to its component studies as independent experiments.

studies.title: Shaping pollinator diversity through coffee agroforestry management: A meta-analytical approach
studies.source_locator: Indexed article sections: methods/results/discussion; supplements not fully extracted
studies.reported_design: Twenty studies, 137 result sets; floral resources, shade and forest distance with ecological/methodological moderators.
studies.reported_results: Local floral resources generally supported bee diversity; shade/forest effects were not uniformly broad and varied with context.
studies.project_interpretation: Diversity is not yield; preserve sampling-method and climate moderators rather than one global management score.

studies.title: Coffee plant–pollinator interactions: a review
studies.source_locator: Indexed article sections: methods/results/discussion; supplements not fully extracted
studies.reported_design: Review of coffee reproductive biology and bee interactions.
studies.reported_results: Discusses evidence that visitor abundance and per-visit effectiveness can differ.
studies.project_interpretation: Use for historical citation discovery; verify original studies before importing numerical effects.

studies.title: Neglected pollinators: Can enhanced pollination services improve cocoa yields? A review
studies.source_locator: Abstract
studies.reported_design: Review of plant/external limitations, pollinator agents and ecological intensification.
studies.reported_results: Identifies pollination as a promising but experimentally unresolved management opportunity.
studies.project_interpretation: Use its reference network to extend coverage; review conclusions are not additional experimental replicates.

studies.title: Protocol to detect and assess pollination deficits in crops: a handbook for its use
studies.source_locator: Handbook contents and overview; annexes not fully extracted
studies.reported_design: Framework for treatment/site design, pollinator observations, production variables and analyses.
studies.reported_results: Methodological guidance, not a new coffee/cacao treatment effect.
studies.project_interpretation: Use as protocol structure and extract the relevant annexes before formal replication.

studies.title: Does the ‘Old Bag’ Make a Good ‘Wind Bag’?: Comparison of Four Fabrics Commonly Used as Exclusion Bags in Studies of Pollination and Reproductive Biology
studies.source_locator: Indexed article sections: methods/results/discussion; supplements not fully extracted
studies.reported_design: Comparison of bag fabrics and pollen penetration.
studies.reported_results: Pollen deposition differed among materials.
studies.project_interpretation: Specify physical aperture and validate ventilation/pollen permeability; insect exclusion does not equal pollen exclusion.

studies.title: Manual pollination techniques and verification of incompatibility: Implementation of selection trials and data collection
studies.source_locator: Institutional repository abstract
studies.reported_design: Controlled self/cross pollination and incompatibility methods, with contamination pitfalls.
studies.reported_results: Incomplete isolation and contaminated instruments can produce unintended fertilizations.
studies.project_interpretation: Require donor chain-of-custody, tool cleaning/drying and isolation events; validate technique before routine field work.

studies.title: Eyes on nature: Embedded vision cameras for terrestrial biodiversity monitoring
studies.source_locator: Article overview; detailed validation not fully extracted
studies.reported_design: Embedded vision with configurable lenses and on-device detection across multiple field applications.
studies.reported_results: Demonstrated flexible observation applications; not validation of our selected Pi camera/lens or local insect species.
studies.project_interpretation: Compare event-triggered versus scheduled sampling and audit missed detections; separate hardware specifications from biological validation.
